_comment: Shared validation fixtures for the TeamDef graph. ONE file, TWO validators.
consumer 1: src/lib/validate.test.ts — the canvas's TypeScript mirror.
consumer 2: loomcycle's internal/teamgraph shared-cases test, which reads
THIS file out of node_modules/@loomboard/workflow/testdata/
once the component is integrated there.
The canvas mirrors teamgraph.Validate so an operator sees a broken graph
while drawing rather than when op=create refuses it. Two implementations of
one rule set drift, silently, and this file is what stops it: a rule added
to validate.go without a case here is a rule the canvas will not surface.
Shipping the fixture in the package (package.json `files`) is what lets the
coupling survive the repo boundary instead of becoming a copy that rots.
go_valid / ts_valid are separate on purpose. They agree everywhere except
where RFC CZ decision 3 requires them not to — an unknown handler kind is an
error to the runtime and merely UNKNOWN to a canvas that may simply be older
than the runtime. Any case where they differ must say why in why_divergent.
VERIFIED: every go_valid below was checked by RUNNING these cases through
loomcycle's own json decoder + teamgraph.Validate — not by hand, and not by
reading the validator. Last run at tag v1.109.0 (2026-10-09): all 242 agree,
and none of the earlier 175 changed its verdict. Decoding counts: several
hook shapes, and a decision question of the wrong JSON type, are refused
while unmarshalling, before Validate runs.
The 67 added on 2026-10-09 are the decision state (loomcycle RFC ED: its
questions, about, route, threshold, and the edges its answers need) and
`capture`, which the runtime checks on every kind and the canvas had not.
That check earned its keep immediately. The `unknown handler kind from a
newer runtime` case used `starter` as its example of a kind the runtime does
not implement. RFC CY L4 then implemented it, and the definition happened to
be a VALID starter — so go_valid silently became wrong, and the divergence
the case exists to document evaporated while the case kept passing. Its kind
is now fictional, which is the only form that cannot decay.
Re-run it after any teamgraph change. The permanent version of this is the
integration test in loomcycle reading this file out of
node_modules/@loomboard/workflow/testdata/, which is what makes the coupling
self-enforcing rather than a thing someone has to remember.

cases.why_divergent: RFC CZ decision 3. The runtime rejects a kind it does not implement, and must. The canvas must NOT: it may be an older build talking to a newer runtime, and refusing to render the kind would push the operator back to hand-editing JSON. The canvas renders it opaque, preserves it byte-for-byte, reports it at info, and lets the server be the authority. The kind here is FICTIONAL on purpose — this case previously used `starter`, which RFC CY L4 then implemented, at which point go_valid became wrong and the divergence this case exists to document silently evaporated. Caught by running the fixtures against teamgraph.Validate.

cases.why_divergent: RFC CZ decision 3, applied to hooks. teamgraph refuses hooks on any kind that does not start runs — and it refuses an unknown kind outright. The canvas cannot know whether a kind newer than itself starts runs, so it applies no hook rule to an opaque node and lets the server decide, as it does for every other rule on that node. The kind is FICTIONAL on purpose (C10).
